evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Bridge over Troubled Water': Simon took the title idea from a line by Claude Jeter in the Swan Silvertones' 1959 gospel record 'Mary Don't You Weep' and set the song on piano to reflect a gospel influence. Franklin recorded it in summer 1970 for 'Young, Gifted and Black', first performed it on 5 March 1971 at the Fillmore West, and Simon has named her version his favourite cover of any song he wrote.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Simon & Garfunkel's version is a slow piano ballad that builds to a huge orchestral ending. Franklin's begins in church: gospel organ and piano, a slower start, and a voice that improvises around the melody instead of singing it as written. Listen for where she leaves Simon's tune entirely and comes back to it.

explanation.age13: Paul Simon got the idea for 'Bridge over Troubled Water' from an old gospel record. Aretha Franklin, who grew up singing gospel in church, recorded it a year later as a gospel song. Simon has said hers is his favourite version of any of his songs.
explanation.adult: A song borrowed from the Black church by a white New York songwriter and taken back to it by a pastor's daughter. The author's own preference for the cover is the evidence the return worked.
